A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAD-GS research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison despite changes in formatting and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Waymo and nuScenes reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations and qualitative geometry results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional comparator results, qualitative outputs and an operation-time measurement.

M1.justification: Equation (3) adds epsilon to the longitudinal-translation denominator for numerical stability, modifying the defined view-selection score. The visibility reasoning, dynamic-object MVS and four-term loss remain unchanged. Subset selection already appeared in v1's appendix; the added optimizer and hyperparameter descriptions do not establish a new component.

E1.justification: Both use the same eight Waymo sequences and six nuScenes scenes, with the same scene exclusions. The single-camera Waymo evaluation and multi-camera qualitative example already appear in v1. Additional visual examples remain within the existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The Waymo comparison adds PVG and OmniRe in v2 Table 1, alongside the five baselines retained from v1 Table 2. These methods already participated in the nuScenes comparison, whose comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The every-fourth-timestamp test split, withholding all associated camera views, camera configurations and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Newly specified method settings are disclosures rather than demonstrated protocol revisions. Removing the 30,000-iteration statement does not establish a changed training budget.

E4.justification: v2 extends the traffic-sign case study with an explicit initial-versus-densified point comparison in Figure 11. Figure 9 also adds depth and normal diagnostics to the existing single-camera Waymo examples. The three component ablations and their supplementary cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Both present point estimates; the retained stochastic view-selection formulation is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The Waymo table changes NSG LPIPS from 21.67 to 0.346, MARS LPIPS from 0.905 to 0.264, and EmerNeRF PSNR*/SSIM from 0.346/0.264 to 21.67/0.905. v2 adds PVG and OmniRe Waymo results, an approximately 48 ms operation time, and qualitative comparison panels. VAD-GS's Waymo scores, all nuScenes table values and quantitative ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (3) revises the mathematical definition of the diversity score by replacing |tz| with |tz| plus epsilon. The Gaussian, compositing, homography and loss equations otherwise remain unchanged, as does the randomized subset objective moved from v1 supplementary Equation (1) to v2 Equation (6). No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions retain the same claims about visibility reasoning, diversity-aware view selection, dynamic MVS and geometry completion. The claimed rendering advantages and central research scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 7.1 explains visibility ambiguity and the role of COLMAP observation tracks. Section 5.3 explicitly acknowledges the lack of ground truth for quantitative completion evaluation along unseen trajectories, while the conclusion clarifies fallback to gradient-based densification for non-rigid objects. The broader deformability and glass/fence limitations already existed in v1.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly specifies depth/opacity thresholds, loss weights, disabling the hard-depth loss after 80% of training, four supporting views, clique optimization and CUDA timing. A project-page pointer replaces the future code-release statement without establishing code availability. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit 30,000-iteration budget and implementation-base attribution.

R1.justification: v2 adds related works including HUGSIM, CoDa-4DGS, Anchored 4D Gaussian Splatting and PlaneStereo, plus classical visibility references. These expand context without fundamentally changing the positioning around visibility-aware geometry completion. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative sequence are retained. v2 introduces numbered sections, separates dataset and implementation descriptions, adds a visibility explanation and revises selected mechanism and conclusion passages. It also expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments and repairs unresolved supplementary citations.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially expanded and reorganized: the Waymo table is transposed, Figure 5 gains another qualitative row, and the former RGB-only Waymo gallery gains depth and normal rows. New Figures 8 and 11, a redrawn multi-camera schematic, and document-wide typography and float-layout changes go beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the paper through corrected Waymo baseline entries, clearer implementation and visibility explanations, repaired citations and stronger qualitative geometry evidence. The principal experiments and conclusions remain stable. Omitting the explicit 30,000-iteration budget partly offsets the added reproducibility details, but the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
